newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed with three early-maturing contracts rising due to active domestic A share trading on the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 10.49 percent from 7.00 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 3.2 million lots from 1.9 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the A share markets performed very actively on Monday with a total turnover of about 23 billion yuan.
"The brisk A share markets were the major factor which fanned short-term fund demand on the repo market, pushing up the early-maturing contracts," said one trader.
One new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange also helped support rates, especially the rate for the seven-day contract, traders said.
Traders said the movement of the repo rates in the next few days would depend on the performance of the A share markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down in dull trading on Monday with the active stock markets sucking funds out of the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 109.14 yuan from 109.45 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 801,509 lots from 924,741 lots.

"Speculative money flowed out into the A share markets with many speculators expecting the stock markets to rebound in the short term," one trader said. "Some liquidated their state debt positions today."
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to consolidate in the next few days.
